subsystems.name: Process payload
subsystems.role: the hardware that actually makes the product — a furnace, crystallisation cell or alloy casting module.

subsystems.name: Host platform
subsystems.role: provides microgravity, power, thermal control and communications.
parts: pressurised rack inside a station module, or a free-flying spacecraft bus

subsystems.name: Return capsule
subsystems.role: protects the product through launch, orbit and the violent trip home.

subsystems.name: Thermal protection system
subsystems.role: absorbs the heat of reentry, which for a low-Earth-orbit return means hitting the atmosphere at roughly 7.8 km/s.
parts: ablative heat shield (phenolic-impregnated carbon ablator type)

subsystems.name: Descent and recovery
subsystems.role: slows the capsule and finds it on the ground.

subsystems.name: Ground segment
subsystems.role: plans the mission, commands the process, and analyses the returned material.

buildSteps.title: Pick a product where gravity gets in the way
buildSteps.detail: Candidates are protein crystals (convection and settling spoil the lattice), fluoride glass fibre such as ZBLAN (Earth-made fibre crystallises, scattering light), and alloys or foams that separate into layers under gravity.

buildSteps.title: Design the process hardware
buildSteps.detail: A sealed cartridge holds the starting material; a programmable furnace cycles temperature over hours or weeks to grow a crystal or draw a fibre without any buoyancy-driven stirring.

buildSteps.title: Qualify for launch and space
buildSteps.detail: The payload is shaken, vacuum-tested and thermal-cycled to survive a rocket ride and the station or free-flyer environment.

buildSteps.title: Launch and install
buildSteps.detail: The payload rides up on a cargo flight and is either installed in a rack on the station or remains in a free-flying capsule.

buildSteps.title: Run the process
buildSteps.detail: Commands from the ground trigger the heating and cooling cycle; sensors record temperature, pressure and any vibration.

buildSteps.title: Stow the product
buildSteps.detail: The finished crystal, fibre spool or alloy sample is secured in the return capsule so it cannot shift or crack during descent.

buildSteps.title: Deorbit and reenter
buildSteps.detail: A small thruster fires to drop the perigee; the heat shield faces the plasma and keeps the inside at room temperature.

buildSteps.title: Descend and recover
buildSteps.detail: Parachutes deploy in the last few kilometres; a recovery team reaches the capsule, often within hours, and moves the product to cold storage or a lab.

buildSteps.title: Compare and qualify
buildSteps.detail: The returned material is measured against Earth-made equivalents; only a clearly better product justifies the launch cost.

prerequisites.why: the loop only closes if payloads can go up and come down on a routine schedule.
the effect needs weeks to months of free fall, not minutes of parabolic flight.
several have flown, but routine, low-cost downmass is new and still proving reliability.

prerequisites.tech: Precision microgravity furnaces and crystallisation hardware
prerequisites.why: temperature control to within a fraction of a degree is what makes the product uniform.

prerequisites.tech: A product worth far more than its launch cost
prerequisites.why: the whole business case rests on price per kilogram high enough to beat Earth-based manufacturing.

pathway.milestone: experiments in the ISS National Lab and the first small commercial capsules returning product — for example a US capsule that landed in Utah in February 2024 carrying crystals of the drug ritonavir, and a Welsh company whose first demonstration satellite was lost in a January 2023 launch failure
pathway.unlocks: proof that the manufacturing-and-return loop physically works.

pathway.milestone: dedicated free-flying manufacturing platforms with their own return vehicles and a repeatable flight cadence
pathway.unlocks: processes that need months of uninterrupted microgravity rather than a station rack.

pathway.milestone: independent laboratory analysis showing space-made fibre or crystals are meaningfully better
pathway.unlocks: real customers instead of demonstration missions.

pathway.milestone: higher-throughput return and eventually larger orbital platforms serving many processes at once
pathway.unlocks: a genuine off-world industrial niche in high-value, low-mass materials.
